subject: maths
card: Names and properties of 2D and 3D shapes, angles, symmetry, perimeter and area.
title: Shapes
seo_title: 2D and 3D shapes practice: angles, symmetry, perimeter and area (KS2)
description: Learn the names and properties of 2D and 3D shapes: polygons, types of angle, triangles and quadrilaterals, lines of symmetry, faces, edges and vertices, and perimeter and area of rectangles. Free practice with pictures for ages 9 to 11.
intro: Shapes are everywhere: in buildings, bridges, footballs and honeycombs. Learn their names, what makes each one special, and how to measure around and inside them.

units.title: Naming 2D shapes
units.blurb: Polygons and how many sides they have.

learn.p: A **polygon** is a flat shape with straight sides. Its name tells you how many sides it has: triangle 3, quadrilateral 4, pentagon 5, hexagon 6, heptagon 7, octagon 8.

A **regular** polygon has all its sides the same length and all its angles the same size. A square is a regular quadrilateral. A rectangle that isn't a square is not regular: its sides are not all equal.
A circle is a 2D shape, but it isn't a polygon, because it has a curved edge and no straight sides.

questions.q: What is this shape called?
questions.hint: Count the sides.
questions.explain: It has 6 sides, so it is a hexagon.

questions.q: What is this shape called?
questions.hint: Count the sides. “Octo” means 8, like an octopus.
questions.explain: It has 8 sides, so it is an octagon.

questions.q: How many sides does a pentagon have?
questions.hint: “Penta” means 5.
questions.explain: A pentagon has 5 sides.

questions.q: Which shape is a regular polygon?
questions.hint: All sides equal and all angles equal.
questions.explain: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 equal angles. A circle isn't a polygon at all.

questions.q: What do you call any shape with 4 straight sides?
questions.hint: “Quad” means 4.
questions.explain: Any 4-sided polygon is a quadrilateral: squares, rectangles, kites and more.

questions.q: How many sides do 3 triangles and 2 hexagons have altogether?

units.title: Angles
units.blurb: Right angles, acute, obtuse and degrees.

learn.p: An angle measures a turn. A whole turn is **360°**. A half turn is 180° and a quarter turn is 90°, which we call a **right angle**. A small square in the corner shows a right angle.
An **acute** angle is less than 90°. An **obtuse** angle is more than 90° but less than 180°. A **reflex** angle is more than 180°.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. Angles all the way round a point add up to 360°.

questions.q: What type of angle is 45°?
questions.hint: Is it less than 90°?
questions.explain: 45° is less than 90°, so it is acute.

questions.q: What type of angle is 120°?
questions.hint: Is it between 90° and 180°?
questions.explain: 120° is more than 90° and less than 180°, so it is obtuse.

questions.q: How many degrees are in a half turn?
questions.hint: A whole turn is 360°.

questions.q: Two angles sit on a straight line. One is 130°. What is the other?
questions.hint: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°.

questions.q: How many right angles make a whole turn?
questions.hint: A right angle is 90°. A whole turn is 360°.
questions.explain: 360 ÷ 90 = 4 right angles.

questions.q: At 3 o'clock, what angle do the hands of a clock make?
questions.hint: From 12 to 3 is a quarter of the way round.
questions.explain: A quarter turn is 90°: a right angle.

questions.q: What type of angle is 250°?
questions.hint: It's more than 180°.
questions.explain: Angles more than 180° (and less than 360°) are reflex.

learn.p: **Equilateral**: 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles (60° each). **Isosceles**: 2 equal sides and 2 equal angles. **Scalene**: no equal sides. **Right-angled**: one angle is 90°. The angles in any triangle add up to 180°.

**Square**: 4 equal sides, 4 right angles. **Rectangle**: 4 right angles, opposite sides equal. **Rhombus**: 4 equal sides, opposite angles equal. **Parallelogram**: opposite sides equal and parallel. **Trapezium**: at least one pair of parallel sides. **Kite**: two pairs of equal sides next to each other.
Two lines are **parallel** if they stay the same distance apart and never meet, like railway tracks.

questions.q: A triangle has 3 equal sides. What kind of triangle is it?
questions.hint: “Equi” means equal.
questions.explain: A triangle with 3 equal sides is equilateral.

questions.q: Two angles in a triangle are 50° and 60°. What is the third angle?
questions.hint: The angles in a triangle add up to 180°.

questions.q: What is this shape?
questions.hint: All 4 sides are the same length, but the angles are not right angles.
questions.explain: 4 equal sides with no right angles: a rhombus.

questions.q: What is this shape?
questions.hint: Only the top and bottom sides are parallel.
questions.explain: One pair of parallel sides: a trapezium.

questions.q: Which shape always has 4 right angles but does not always have 4 equal sides?
questions.hint: Think of a door shape.
questions.explain: A rectangle always has 4 right angles, but its sides don't all have to be equal.

questions.q: An isosceles triangle has one angle of 40° and two equal angles. How big is each of the equal angles?
questions.hint: 180 − 40 is shared equally between the other two angles.

units.title: Lines of symmetry
units.blurb: Fold it so both halves match.

learn.p: A **line of symmetry** splits a shape into two halves that match exactly, like a mirror image. If you folded the shape along the line, the halves would fit perfectly on top of each other.
A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry (across the middle both ways, but not the diagonals). A square has 4. An equilateral triangle has 3.
A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as it has sides. A regular hexagon has 6. A circle has an endless number!

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.hint: Across both ways, and both diagonals.
questions.explain: 2 lines through the middles of the sides and 2 diagonals: 4.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle (that isn't a square) have?
questions.hint: Try folding a piece of paper along a diagonal. Do the halves match?
questions.explain: Only the two lines across the middle. The diagonals don't work: the halves don't fit on top of each other.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does a regular pentagon have?
questions.hint: A regular polygon has as many lines of symmetry as sides.
questions.explain: 5 sides, 5 lines of symmetry.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does this kite have?
questions.hint: Try a line from the top point to the bottom point.
questions.explain: Only the line from top to bottom works: 1 line of symmetry.

questions.q: How many lines of symmetry does an isosceles triangle (that isn't equilateral) have?
questions.hint: The line goes down the middle, between the two equal sides.
questions.explain: 1 line, from the top down through the middle of the base.

questions.q: Which capital letter has a line of symmetry?
questions.hint: Imagine a mirror down the middle of each letter.
questions.explain: A has a vertical line of symmetry. F, G and J have none.

learn.p: A **face** is a flat surface. An **edge** is where two faces meet. A **vertex** is a corner (more than one: **vertices**).

**Cube**: 6 square faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices. **Cuboid** (like a box): 6 rectangular faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices. **Square-based pyramid**: 5 faces, 8 edges, 5 vertices. **Triangular prism** (like a tent): 5 faces, 9 edges, 6 vertices.
A **sphere** (a ball) has one curved surface. A **cylinder** (a tin can) has 2 flat circular faces and one curved surface.

questions.q: How many faces does a cube have?
questions.hint: Think of a dice.
questions.explain: A cube (like a dice) has 6 faces.

questions.q: How many vertices does a cube have?
questions.hint: Count the corners: 4 on top, 4 on the bottom.
questions.explain: 4 + 4 = 8 vertices.

questions.q: How many edges does a cuboid have?
questions.hint: 4 round the top, 4 round the bottom, 4 going up the sides.

questions.q: Which 3D shape has 5 faces: a square base and 4 triangles?
questions.hint: Like the pyramids in Egypt.
questions.explain: A square-based pyramid has 1 square face and 4 triangular faces.

questions.q: A tin of beans is the shape of a…
questions.hint: Two circles joined by a curved surface.
questions.explain: A tin is a cylinder: 2 flat circles and a curved surface.

questions.q: How many faces does a triangular prism have?
questions.hint: 2 triangles at the ends and rectangles round the sides.
questions.explain: 2 triangles + 3 rectangles = 5 faces.

units.title: Perimeter and area
units.blurb: The distance around, and the space inside.

learn.p: The **perimeter** is the distance all the way around the outside. For a rectangle 5 cm by 3 cm: 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 cm.
The **area** is how much space is inside, measured in squares. A rectangle 5 cm by 3 cm holds 3 rows of 5 squares: 5 × 3 = 15 square centimetres (15 cm²).
Perimeter is a length (cm, m). Area is squares (cm², m²). Two shapes can have the same area but different perimeters!

questions.q: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 6 cm long and 4 cm wide?
questions.hint: Add all four sides: 6 + 4 + 6 + 4.

questions.q: What is the area of a rectangle 6 cm long and 4 cm wide?
questions.hint: Length × width.

questions.q: A square has sides of 7 m. What is its perimeter?
questions.hint: 4 equal sides.

questions.q: A square has sides of 7 m. What is its area?
A rectangle has an area of 30 cm². It is 5 cm wide. How long is it?
A garden is 10 m long and 8 m wide. How many metres of fence go all the way round it?
questions.hint: This is the perimeter.

questions.q: Shape A is 6 cm by 2 cm. Shape B is 4 cm by 3 cm. Which is true?
questions.hint: Work out both areas and both perimeters.
questions.explain: Areas: 6 × 2 = 12 and 4 × 3 = 12, the same. Perimeters: 16 cm and 14 cm, different.
